underground_design.mining_method: Sublevel open stoping, sublevel caving in some areas
underground_design.stope_dimensions: 20m x 10m x 15m (L x W x H)
underground_design.support_system: Rock bolts 2.4m, shotcrete 100mm, cable bolts in weak zones

key_lessons: Shale layers are weak and require additional support
Bedding-parallel structures control failure modes
Deep mining creates high-stress conditions
Backfill essential for regional stability
Seismic monitoring critical for rockburst prediction
challenges: Very weak shale horizons requiring heavy support
High vertical stress at depth (>1500m)
Complex structural geology with multiple shear zones
Water management in deep workings
Rockburst potential in competent rock units

hoek_brown_parameters.description: Intact rock constant mi for Hoek-Brown failure criterion

mapping.description: Detailed geological mapping of surface exposures

borehole_drilling.core_logging: RQD, fracture frequency, lithology, alteration, weathering

geophysical_surveys.purpose: Identify structural features, voids, water-bearing zones
geophysical_surveys.resolution: Depends on method and survey spacing

test_pitting_and_trenching.description: Excavation of test pits and trenches for shallow investigation
test_pitting_and_trenching.purpose: Soil characterization, weathering profile, shallow structure

durability_index.method: Slake durability test with repeated cycles

swelling_test.method: Free swell or confined swell test

creep_test.method: Constant load test over extended period

underground_openings.pillar_stability: Factor of safety >= 1.5-2.0 depending on consequences

rockburst_classification.strain_burst: Shallow depth, high stress concentration, brittle failure
rockburst_classification.face_burst: Ahead of advancing face, stress redistribution
rockburst_classification.fault_slip: Triggered by stress change on existing fault

design_criteria.design_event: 1 in 100 year event for permanent openings
design_criteria.dynamic_amplification: Factor of 2-3 for corner zones and intersections

sources: Hoek and Brown (1997) - Underground Excavations in Rock
Australian Geomechanics Society (2000) - Landslide Risk Management
limitations: Values are typical ranges, site-specific data required for design
Rock mass properties are inherently variable
Classification systems are empirical and have limitations
Design should be verified by experienced geotechnical engineers
Instrumentation and monitoring essential for validating design assumptions
recommendations: Always use site-specific geotechnical data for design
Engage qualified geotechnical engineers for critical design
Implement comprehensive instrumentation and monitoring programs
Regularly review and update geotechnical models as new data becomes available
Apply observational method for uncertain ground conditions
